messages.content: You check whether the evidence collected so far is enough to answer a question about a scientific paper. Say sufficient only if, for EVERY sub-question, some evidence item contains the specific fact, number or picture that answers it -- not merely the same topic. The fact must BE the answer: for 'which X' it names the X; for 'how does A affect B' or 'what is the effect of A' it states the direction or size of the change; for 'how many' or 'what value' it gives the number. A fact that only restates the question or describes the topic does not answer it. First give, for each sub-question you can answer, the id of the item (E1, E2, ...) and the answering fact in a few words; then list the numbers of the sub-questions still uncovered, say in a few words what is missing, and only then decide.

Question: What is the difference between testing domain adaptation and testing sensor fusion?
Sub-questions:
1. [figure] What is the difference between testing domain adaptation and testing sensor fusion?
Evidence:
E1 [figure, Figure 1, page 2] (image attached): Fig. 1. We propose zero-shot deep domain adaptation (ZDDA) for domain adapta- tion and sensor fusion. ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable. In this example domain adaptation task (MNIST [27] → MNIST-M [13]), the task-irrelevant gray-RGB pairs are from the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset and the Fashion-MNIST-M dataset (the colored version of the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset with the details in Sec. 4.1)
Words printed in the figure: 2 K.-C. Peng, Z. Wu, and J. Ernst
E2 [figure, Figure 1, page 2]: Zoomed view (300 dpi) of: Fig. 1. We propose zero-shot deep domain adaptation (ZDDA) for domain adapta- tion and sensor fusion. ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable. In this example domain adaptation task (MNIST [27] → MNIST-M [13]), the task-irrelevant gray-RGB pairs are from the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset and the Fashion-MNIST-M dataset (the colored version of the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset with the details in Sec. 4.1)
Words printed in the figure: 2 K.-C. Peng, Z. Wu, and J. Ernst [image]
